dublinCore.description: Interactive comparison of the classic analog low-pass prototypes (Butterworth, Chebyshev I, Chebyshev II, elliptic and Bessel) at the same order: magnitude in dB on a log frequency axis with a passband zoom, phase, group delay, step response and s-plane poles and zeros, plus a table of passband edge, stopband edge, transition width, selectivity ratio, overshoot and 2% settling time for each family.
relation: Chapter 10: Advanced Filter Design and Implementation

topic: Butterworth, Chebyshev, elliptic and Bessel approximations
learningObjectives: Compare the transition width (omega_s - omega_p) of the five prototype families at the same order and rank them from sharpest to gentlest
Relate the pole and zero pattern in the s-plane (a circle, an ellipse, poles close to the j-omega axis, zeros on the j-omega axis) to flatness, ripple and notches in the magnitude response
Analyze the trade-off between frequency selectivity and time-domain behavior: overshoot, settling time and group-delay variation
Calculate Butterworth band edges and the minimum Butterworth order from |H|^2 = 1/(1 + omega^(2N)), and check them against the read-outs
Evaluate which prototype best meets an application requirement, such as sharp channel selection or faithful pulse shape
prerequisites: Decibels, step response and group delay
Filter specifications: passband, stopband and transition band

misconceptions.misconception: The sharpest filter is the best filter
misconceptions.correction: Sharp transitions come from poles close to the j-omega axis, which cause large overshoot, long settling and group-delay peaks
misconceptions.evidence: At the default settings the elliptic filter has the narrowest transition (0.496 rad/s) but the largest overshoot (24.0%) and longest settling time (23.12 s); at N = 8 its transition is 0.022 rad/s and it settles in 57.73 s

misconceptions.misconception: Chebyshev II gives up selectivity to get a flat passband
misconceptions.correction: Chebyshev I and II have the same selectivity ratio for the same N, Rp and As; Type II moves the equiripple behavior to the stopband
misconceptions.evidence: With 'Passband edge at omega = 1 rad/s' scaling both Chebyshev rows show omega_s = 2.339, while Chebyshev II overshoots 13.0% instead of 21.9%

accessibility.screenReaderScript: Five classic analog low-pass filter prototypes compared at the same order: a magnitude plot in dB on a log frequency axis, phase, group delay, step response, an s-plane pole-zero plot, and a table of passband edge, stopband edge, transition width, overshoot and settling time for each family. Checkboxes show or hide Butterworth, Chebyshev I, Chebyshev II, elliptic and Bessel designs; sliders set the order, the passband ripple and the stopband attenuation.

model.description: Builds each analog low-pass prototype as pole and zero lists, scales it in frequency so that the -3.01 dB point or the passband edge lies at 1 rad/s, and evaluates the frequency response, phase, group delay and step response analytically from the poles and zeros
equations: H(s) = K prod(s - z_i) / prod(s - p_k)
Chebyshev I: |H(jw)|^2 = 1 / (1 + eps^2 T_N^2(w)), eps = sqrt(10^(Rp/10) - 1)
Chebyshev II: |H(jw)|^2 = T_N^2(1/w) / (eps_s^2 + T_N^2(1/w)), eps_s = sqrt(10^(As/10) - 1)
Elliptic: |H(jw)|^2 = 1 / (1 + eps^2 R_N^2(w)), degree equation K'(k)/K(k) = K'(k1) / (N K(k1)), k1 = eps / eps_s
Bessel: H(s) = theta_N(0) / theta_N(s), reverse Bessel polynomial
group delay tau(w) = sum_k sigma_k / (sigma_k^2 + (w - w_k)^2) for poles p_k = -sigma_k + j w_k
step response y(t) = H(0) + Re sum_k (Res_{p_k} H / p_k) e^{p_k t}
algorithms: Landen transformations for the Jacobi elliptic functions sn and cd
Durand-Kerner root finding for the Bessel polynomial
Bisection for the frequency scaling and the band edges

instructionalStrategies: Rank the families by transition width, then by overshoot, and discuss the reversal
Compare the two scalings to separate selectivity from absolute band edges
Link each feature of the magnitude response to the pole-zero plot
extensions: Add the bilinear transform to map each prototype to a digital IIR filter and compare the warped band edges
Add an order-estimation mode that finds the minimum N of each family for a given omega_p, omega_s, Rp and As
